svg.metadata: {"config":"default","device":"Smartoptics DCP-R-34D-CS","device-version":"5.0.1","generator":{"tool":"portrayal-render","version":"0.1.0"},"resolved-components":{"common/laser-warning@1":"1.0.0","common/lc-duplex-adapter@6":"6.0.1","common/lc-dust-cap@1":"1.0.1","common/led-dot@1":"1.1.0","common/rj45-eth@1":"1.2.0","std/lc-bulkhead-bore@1":"1.0.1","std/rj45@2":"2.1.0","std/sfp@1":"1.4.1"},"source":{"attrs":{"performance":{"channels":34}},"chassis":{"color":"#1b1e21","depth":505,"height":45,"ru":1,"width":440},"description":"34-channel colourless/directionless cross-connect ROADM line unit, 1RU. Two rows of LC duplex adapters (XC01-XC34) plus Line, 1510 OSC filter and OSC monitor, with ETH0 and RS232 management.","format":1,"groups":{"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"line":{"description":"the line side, as opposed to the add/drop channels and the cross-connects: the DWDM Line port, the 1510 filter that splits the optical supervisory channel off it, and the SFP that terminates that channel.","index-origin":1,"mixed":"TWO CONNECTOR FAMILIES, ONE JOB. Line and 1510 are LC duplex adapters and the OSC is an SFP cage, so the block declares no media of its own and each port carries its own. They are grouped by what they are FOR - everything facing the line, rather than the channels added and dropped from it - and splitting them by connector would put the filter and the transceiver it feeds in different blocks, which is the one relationship a reader of this face needs to see.","role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the unit's management interfaces, on both faces. REAR - ETH1-4 on RJ45 to the shelf controller, ETH5 as an SFP for optical management access, and the recessed reset beside them; DCP-R User Manual 14.0 A section 2.10 lists those as one set of network management interfaces. FRONT - ETH0 on RJ45 and the RS-232 craft console, which were in no group at all and so drew a row each beside the port groups. Two blocks, one job, and the tree separates them by view without needing two words","role":"management","term":"Port"},"port-leds":{"description":"every indicator that belongs to a particular port, ordered by that port","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"status-leds":{"description":"the chassis indicators, which report the unit rather than any one port","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"xc":{"attrs":{"media":"fiber","role":"cross-connect"},"description":"XC01-XC34, the cross-connect ports. One block of 34 laid out seventeen over seventeen - the two rows are how they fit on a 1U faceplate, not two kinds of port","index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"Smartoptics","maturity":"modelled","model":"DCP-R-34D-CS","name":"dcp-r-34d-cs","profile":"optical","provenance":{"brand-position":{"confidence":"measured","note":"measured off the stencil art - smartoptics runs 6.1 to 27.3mm from the body edge and the model name 29.9 to 49.6, both well left of the first port. Decor text anchors on its CENTRE, so these carry the mid-point of each measured span, not its left edge - anchoring the edge value ran the brand off the side of the chassis"},"chassis":{"note":"manual DIMENSIONS (DCP-R) - 440mm (W) x 45mm (H) x 505mm (D), 1 RU. The manual also states power and fan units are in the back panel, so this is a standalone chassis and not a plug-in unit"},"column-grid":{"note":"top and bottom rows agreed to within 0.15mm across all 17 columns, so a single averaged grid is used and the drawing jitter discarded"},"markings":{"note":"photo - IEC 60825 laser hazard triangles in the gap between the two port blocks, one above the top row and one below the bottom"},"mgmt-jack-alignment":{"note":"stencil art, correcting the ShapeSheet. The connection points put ETH0's centre at 17.49 and RS232's at 17.94, and the model transcribed both - but the art draws the two shells flush, left edges within 0.17mm of each other, so that 0.45 is drafting jitter in hand-placed Visio dots rather than a real step. Both jacks now sit on one x of 17.7, the mean of the two readings. Same treatment `column-grid` already gives the XC columns"},"osc-captions":{"note":"stencil art. The Tx and Rx captions beside the OSC LEDs sat at 30.6 and 42.6, which put Tx 4.3mm from its own LED and Rx 1.9mm from its own on the other side, and threw the pair 1.35mm left of the cage they label. The LEDs themselves were never wrong - measured at 34.88 and 40.77 against the model's 34.9 and 40.7. Captions moved to 31.8 and 43.8, which is where the art puts the text and is symmetric about the cage centre at 37.95"},"port-pairing":{"note":"each LC duplex adapter carries two connection points 6.6mm apart (the Tx and Rx fibers); adapters were recovered by pairing those"},"port-positions":{"note":"stencil ShapeSheet connection points. Visio stores these as FRACTIONS of shape width/height, so they survive without knowing the drawing scale - resolved against the 19-inch rack width the master is drawn at, then expressed from the body edge. ADAPTER BODIES MOVED, FIBRES DID NOT (common/lc-duplex-adapter@6, B3): that adapter's ferrule axis sits 5.82 from its latch-side edge where @4's sat at 5.5, so every placement of it here moved 0.32 toward its own latch side - up on an unturned row, down on a row at rotate 180, with the panel cutout of the same id - and each fibre stays on the position read above."},"port-speeds":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"the OSC cage is `1g`: the DCP-R user manual (14.0), Supported OSC transceivers, certifies SFPs from 155 Mb/s STM-1/Fast Ethernet parts up to 1GE ones, and its OTDR section offers the combined OSC/OTDR SFP at 155 Mb/s or 1 Gb/s. The highest native rate the cage runs at is therefore 1G."},"psu-orientation":{"note":"photo - both modules are fitted the same way round, fan inboard of the inlet, so the C14 sits at the far right on PSU-2 and inboard on PSU-1. They are not mirrored"},"psu-part":{"note":"label - Gospower G1251-0550WNA, P/N CRPS0550-AH, and the fan sticker reads 550W Platinum CRPS. So the module is a standard CRPS 1U part at 73.5 x 40 x 185, not the 84mm-wide estimate taken from the racked photo, and both bays sit flush to the chassis edges"},"rear-layout":{"note":"photo IMG_2181 of racked DCP-R units - PSU with integrated fan and C14 inlet at each end, mirrored; honeycomb vent panel across the centre; management block right of centre. Block positions are approximate to about 3mm - the photo has uncorrected perspective and partial cable occlusion, so it fixes the structure and order but not exact millimetres"},"rear-mgmt-block":{"note":"stencil master dcp-r-rear, which is orthographic - a 2x2 ganged RJ45 shell (ETH 2 / ETH 4 over ETH 1 / ETH 3), ESD warning, Tx and Rx LEDs, an ETH 5 SFP cage and a recessed RESET button"},"side-top-bottom":{"note":"IMG_2188 shows the lid, so these now carry the real finish - a light silver body with the black front panel wrapping about 12.7mm (half an inch) back along every face. Still no vents, screws or lid labels - the photo shows the finish and the panel depth but not those details, so they are left out rather than invented"},"silkscreen":{"note":"port grouping read from the stencil master - XC1 alone, then eight abutting pairs at 13.24mm with about 17.3mm between pairs. Label text corrected from a rack photo - the device prints XC1, not the stencil's XC01, and every port carries a small Tx/Rx box between its name and the adapter, reversed on the bottom row"},"status-leds":{"note":"stencil art - the Power and Status LEDs are 6.11mm apart (centres 54.70 and 60.81), not the 5.6 the model carried. At 5.6 the two captions were 0.2mm apart at font-size 2.0 and rendered as the single word \"PowerStatus\". Correcting the LED pitch fixes the collision without touching the type size, because the captions are centred on their own LEDs"},"tx-rx-drawn":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"THE TWO FIGURES THE MEASURED CENTRES ARE DRAWN WITH, neither read off a source. The FRAME HEIGHT is 2.5, a drawn size where the stencil's box is 1.8: only its centre is the stencil's (`tx-rx-positions`). The NAME BASELINES are placed from the measured glyph centre by taking the cap height as 0.72 of the font size - an assumed ratio, not a measured one - so a baseline is as good as that ratio, while the glyph centre it is derived from is measured"},"tx-rx-positions":{"confidence":"measured","note":"THE CENTRES, MEASURED - and only the centres; the figures drawn around them are `tx-rx-drawn`. Stencil master r-34d-cs, read at 8.86 px/mm (its two XC ferrule rows stand 102.0 px apart against the 11.5 row pitch), each figure measured outward from the art's own ferrule line. The white Tx/Rx box runs 7.96 to 9.76 from the ferrule on the top XC row and 7.62 to 9.42 on the bottom row, 6.49 to 8.18 at 1510 and 7.72 to 9.53 at Line; the port name's glyphs run 10.27 to 12.30 (top), 10.38 to 12.42 (bottom), 8.69 to 10.61 (1510) and 10.04 to 12.07 (Line). Each frame is centred on the box's centre, its divider and Tx/Rx text move with it, and each name's glyph is centred on the stencil name's centre. Until B3 the frames were generated from each adapter's placement 5.85 from the ferrule, about 2 closer than the stencil draws them, and once the adapter bodies moved to keep the fibres on the connection points (common/lc-duplex-adapter@6) the bodies met them. The boxed style, the reversal on the bottom row and the text are the rack photograph's, as `silkscreen` says; only the positions are the stencil's"},"xc-orientation":{"note":"stencil master r-34d-cs - THE BOTTOM ROW IS MIRRORED, latch tongues down against the top row's up. This drawing already knew: every bottom-row port prints its Tx/Rx box reversed, which is only true of a row turned over, and `silkscreen` below has said so since the model was built. It could not be DRAWN until std/lc-bore@3 made the bore keyed (#126) - a 4.7 square has no orientation, so both rows rendered identically and the defect was invisible. Each bottom-row adapter now carries rotate: 180"}},"references":[{"title":"Smartoptics DCP-R User Manual 14.0_A"},{"title":"Smartoptics DCP-R Visio stencil DCP-R_v260105.vssx (master
